paths.description: Homepage and global navigation, representing the entry point, site purpose, login affordance, news and fandom discovery.
Recent Works listing, representing dense browse and result-card templates.
Advanced Work Search plus a completed query for test, representing the primary find-a-work form and results journey.
A current public work, representing the core reading/detail template, work metadata and guest comment surface.
A current AO3 News article, representing editorial content on mobile.
A deliberately missing URL, representing HTTP error and recovery behavior.

findings.summary: The site ignores the user’s dark color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-mode screenshot is pixel-identical to the light desktop view; the preference probe reports colorScheme normal and body background rgb(255, 255, 255) while prefers-color-scheme: dark matches.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide preference-driven dark surface, text, border and control colors with prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: Cross-document navigation changes abruptly with no View Transition support.
findings.evidence: DOM and stylesheet probes found no @view-transition rule or view-transition CSS on the representative MPA templates.
findings.suggestedFix: Add @view-transition { navigation: auto } with restrained transitions, and disable non-essential motion under prefers-reduced-motion.

findings.summary: Long pages provide no scroll-state-aware orientation.
findings.evidence: The 4,613 px mobile search-results page and 3,306 px work detail keep static global chrome and expose no scroll-state queries or progress affordance.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a lightweight progress or condensed sticky navigation treatment on long result and reading templates, using scroll-state queries where support permits.

findings.summary: Menus and overlays use legacy manually positioned dropdown/modal markup.
findings.evidence: DOM inspection shows .dropdown-menu and custom #modal-wrap/#modal elements, with no anchor-name, position-anchor or position-try usage.
findings.suggestedFix: Use popover and CSS anchor positioning with position-try fallbacks for transient menus and tooltips.

findings.summary: Custom div-based overlays replace semantic dialog and popover primitives.
findings.evidence: The rendered DOM contains custom #modal-bg, #modal-wrap and #modal while the probe reports zero dialog, popover and details elements.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace modal divs with dialog for modal flows and popover for transient UI, preserving focus, Escape and light-dismiss behavior.

findings.summary: Responsive behavior relies on viewport styles rather than component-level adaptation.
findings.evidence: Stylesheet inspection found no @container rules even though cards, forms and navigation modules are reused across wide and narrow contexts.
findings.suggestedFix: Introduce container-type on reusable modules and size-aware @container rules where component context differs from viewport size.

findings.summary: Many mobile controls and links have touch targets substantially below 44 by 44 CSS pixels.
findings.evidence: The 360 px target probe lists primary navigation at 26 px high, Search at 22 px, news links at 13 to 16 px and footer links at 12 to 28 px.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase interactive hit areas to at least 44 by 44 CSS pixels through padding and spacing while preserving visible focus styles.

findings.summary: The homepage ships substantial unused legacy JavaScript and CSS.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 53 KiB unused JavaScript in jQuery UI 1.10.0 (89.9 percent unused) and 17 KiB unused CSS (85.3 percent); HAR attributes 94,109 transferred bytes to the Google CDN.
findings.suggestedFix: Load only the jQuery UI modules needed per template, remove obsolete dependencies, and split or conditionally load page-specific CSS and scripts.

findings.summary: The Bluesky follow button fails WCAG AA text contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured 3.61:1 for 12.25 px white text on #1185fe; 4.5:1 is required.
findings.suggestedFix: Darken the button background or enlarge and embolden the label until the computed contrast meets WCAG AA.

findings.summary: The homepage heading hierarchy skips a level.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse flags the account module h4 after the page h2 as invalid heading order.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a heading level that follows the surrounding document outline, and verify the hierarchy on every shared template.

findings.summary: Mobile reflow succeeds, but target sizing does not remain comfortably operable.
findings.evidence: Layout evidence shows no horizontal overflow at 360 px, while the target probe finds dozens of active controls below 44 px high.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep the successful fluid reflow and increase touch target padding and separation across navigation, result cards and footer links.

findings.summary: The shared logo lacks intrinsic dimensions and is too low-resolution for its rendered size at common device pixel ratios.
findings.evidence: The images primitive reports missing width and height; Lighthouse expects about 80 by 56 pixels but receives 61 by 42, and the image contributes a small observed layout shift.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide width and height attributes and an appropriately sized responsive source, preferably an SVG or higher-density raster.

findings.summary: The page depends on stale libraries and a third-party script emitting deprecated API warnings.
findings.evidence: The DOM loads jQuery 1.9.0 and jQuery UI 1.10.0; Lighthouse reports three deprecations from Cloudflare challenge code.
findings.suggestedFix: Upgrade or remove legacy libraries, audit vulnerable transitive code, and coordinate with the edge provider to eliminate deprecated browser APIs.

findings.summary: Detail and article templates do not provide page-specific meta descriptions.
findings.evidence: The sampled work has a descriptive title but repeats the generic site description rather than summarizing the visible work.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate concise, safe page-specific descriptions from public metadata, respecting author privacy and content-warning rules.

findings.summary: Public pages lack canonical links and the expected sitemap endpoint returns 404.
findings.evidence: Home and sampled work probes found no rel=canonical; /sitemap.xml returned HTTP 404 while robots.txt defines crawler-specific policy.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish canonical URLs for public templates and provide segmented sitemaps that honor robots and content-visibility policy.

findings.summary: Public works and news lack structured data and social-preview metadata.
findings.evidence: The sampled work probe found no JSON-LD and no Open Graph tags despite representing a rich creative work entity.
findings.suggestedFix: Add privacy-safe schema.org CreativeWork or Article JSON-LD and Open Graph metadata aligned with visible content and warnings.

findings.summary: Transport defenses and session-cookie settings are incomplete.
findings.evidence: Headers show no HSTS, CSP is limited to frame-ancestors, and _otwarchive_session is HttpOnly and SameSite=Lax but lacks Secure.
findings.suggestedFix: Mark the session cookie Secure, deploy HSTS after subdomain review, and expand CSP beyond clickjacking protection with nonces or hashes for scripts.

findings.summary: Sign-in exposes password authentication without a phishing-resistant passkey path.
findings.evidence: The login DOM contains username and password controls but no WebAuthn or passkey affordance; no permission prompt fired on load.
findings.suggestedFix: Add passkey registration and authentication as a first-class option while retaining accessible account recovery.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced policy coverage is partial.
findings.evidence: Clickjacking, nosniff and Referrer-Policy are present, but HSTS and Permissions-Policy are absent and CSP only defines frame-ancestors.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a restrictive Permissions-Policy, HSTS, and a complete CSP after measuring required origins and inline-script migration.

findings.summary: The stylesheet remains heavily dependent on physical left and right properties.
findings.evidence: CSS captured by the DOM primitive contains 95 physical left/right declarations versus 12 logical inline declarations; html has lang=en but no explicit dir.
findings.suggestedFix: Set dir and migrate layout-sensitive rules to logical margin, padding, border and inset properties, then test RTL content.

findings.summary: Dates are rendered in fixed English or ISO-style text rather than user-locale-aware markup.
findings.evidence: Representative pages expose text such as 20 Jul 2026 and 2026-07-20 without time datetime semantics or evidence of locale-aware formatting.
findings.suggestedFix: Render dates through a locale-aware formatter and expose machine-readable datetime values in time elements.

findings.summary: Authentication and guest-input fields use incomplete autocomplete semantics.
findings.evidence: The username field uses autocomplete=on, while password, guest name and guest email fields omit purpose-specific tokens.
findings.suggestedFix: Use username and current-password for sign-in, plus name and email tokens for guest comments; use new-password only in account creation.

findings.summary: The account flow relies on password-only authentication.
findings.evidence: The public login surface has no passkey registration, authentication or management affordance, leaving a phishing-prone credential as the only visible method.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer passkeys with clear fallback and recovery, and require proportionate reauthentication for sensitive account actions.

findings.summary: Shared decorative and brand images use legacy PNG assets without responsive alternatives.
findings.evidence: The images primitive finds one PNG logo with no responsive source; HAR also transfers a 13,314-byte PNG texture on every homepage load.
findings.suggestedFix: Prefer vector or modern responsive assets and retain explicit dimensions; cache shared decorative assets aggressively.

findings.summary: A third-party legacy script pair consumes nearly half the homepage transfer budget.
findings.evidence: HAR records 94,109 of 206,994 bytes from ajax.googleapis.com, dominated by jQuery and jQuery UI, with no known tracker detected.
findings.suggestedFix: Self-host a minimized, integrity-controlled subset or remove the dependency and defer non-critical code by template.
